security_audit.summary: All 57 static findings are false positives involving documentation formatting, legitimate Firebase tooling, official URLs, and mobile development terminology. One semantic privacy finding concerns mandatory agent metadata telemetry without explicit approval or enforced debug-build guards. No evidence found of credential theft, attacker-controlled destinations, or audit-directed prompt injection.

remediation.issue: Verification uploads agent, model, and workflow metadata without explicit approval or enforced debug-build guards.
remediation.suggestion: Use a minimal test event without agent metadata by default. Require explicit approval, a test Analytics property, and debug-build guards for optional diagnostic telemetry.

semantic_findings.title: Verification Uploads Agent Metadata Without Explicit Approval
semantic_findings.description: The guides require gaac_app_open events containing actual agent names, model names, skill versions, and modified event names. Verification runs automatically and transmits these details to the configured Analytics property without an explicit approval step. Examples lack enforced debug-build guards; later cleanup cannot retract uploaded metadata.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: All four references explicitly require agent and model metadata in temporary Analytics events; setup guides require automatic verification and describe uploads. Debug-only wording and cleanup reduce persistence, but provide neither an approval gate nor a build-time guard.

content.user_title: Integrate Firebase Analytics on Android and iOS
content.value_statement: Mobile analytics setup can fail because of configuration mismatches and missed navigation events. This skill guides SDK integration, screen tracking, and event verification across Android and iOS.
actual_capabilities: Guide Android SDK integration using Kotlin or Java and Kotlin DSL or Groovy Gradle configuration.
Guide iOS SDK integration using Swift Package Manager or CocoaPods, including SwiftUI and UIKit initialization.
Generate a screen inventory and tracking plan with file paths and completion status.
Implement manual screen events for Compose navigation, pagers, Voyager, SwiftUI views, and UIKit controllers.
Explain duplicate-event prevention when automatic screen reporting is enabled.
Guide local event verification through ADB, Logcat, simulator launch arguments, and Firebase DebugView.
limitations: Requires an existing mobile project, Firebase app registration, configuration files, and a linked Google Analytics property.
Live verification requires a suitable device or simulator, platform build tools, network access, and Firebase console access.
Standalone Firebase login, project creation, and configuration downloads are delegated to the separate firebase-basics skill.
Verification instructions include agent metadata telemetry; review approval, consent requirements, and debug-build isolation before use.

use_cases.title: Add Android Analytics
use_cases.description: Integrate the Analytics dependency, match application identifiers, handle build variants, and verify initialization.

use_cases.title: Track iOS Navigation
use_cases.description: Inventory SwiftUI and UIKit screens, implement appropriate screen events, and avoid duplicate automatic reporting.

use_cases.title: Validate Mobile Instrumentation
use_cases.description: Review tracking coverage, inspect local event logs, and check cleanup of temporary verification events and debug settings.

prompt_templates.title: Check Integration Prerequisites
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my [Android or iOS] project for Firebase Analytics prerequisites. List missing dependencies, configuration files, and identifier mismatches before making changes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: assess readiness for the first integration.

prompt_templates.title: Configure the SDK
prompt_templates.prompt: Add Firebase Analytics to my [platform] project using [build system]. Preserve existing initialization and request approval before running tools or uploading diagnostic metadata.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: configure dependencies and initialize Analytics.

prompt_templates.title: Implement Screen Tracking
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a screen inventory for my [navigation framework] app. Propose tracking changes, identify duplicate-reporting risks, and request approval before instrumenting sensitive or vendor screens.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: plan and implement navigation instrumentation.

prompt_templates.title: Verify a Combined Integration
prompt_templates.prompt: Review SDK setup and screen tracking across [build variants or targets]. Verify approved test events, omit agent metadata, and report build results and debug cleanup.

output_examples.input: Review Analytics setup for an Android app with a separate debug application identifier.
output: Configuration review: the debug identifier needs a matching Firebase app registration.
Recommended change: place the matching configuration in the debug source directory.
Verification plan: build the debug variant and inspect approved events in Logcat and DebugView.

output_examples.input: Plan screen tracking for an app using both SwiftUI and UIKit.
output: Tracking inventory: list each navigation destination, its implementation file, and its current reporting method.
Implementation plan: add manual SwiftUI events and retain UIKit automatic reporting where appropriate.
Validation checklist: check duplicate events, confirm approved screen names, and remove temporary diagnostic events.

best_practices: Match configuration files to the active application identifier, build variant, or Xcode target before testing.
Approve screen coverage and event parameters before instrumentation; exclude sensitive values and unnecessary agent metadata.
Verify events in a test environment, then remove temporary event code and disable debug settings.
anti_patterns: Adding manual native screen events without checking whether automatic reporting already tracks those screens.
Uploading diagnostic agent metadata or sensitive screen details without explicit approval and appropriate consent controls.
Copying configuration or dependency settings between variants and targets without checking identifiers and compatibility.

faq.question: Which platforms does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers Android with Kotlin or Java and iOS with Swift or Objective-C, including Compose, SwiftUI, and UIKit tracking patterns.

faq.question: Does this skill create a Firebase project?
faq.answer: Project creation, CLI login, and standalone configuration downloads are delegated to firebase-basics. Analytics integration assumes the required project and app registration exist.

faq.question: Can it track Compose and SwiftUI navigation?
faq.answer: Yes. The references provide manual tracking patterns for Compose navigation and SwiftUI views, which require coverage beyond native automatic screen reporting.

faq.question: How are events verified?
faq.answer: The guides use local debug logs, Android ADB properties, iOS simulator launch arguments, and Firebase DebugView. Verification requires a working development environment.

faq.question: Does verification send agent information?
faq.answer: The references request a temporary event containing agent, model, and workflow metadata. Obtain approval or omit these fields before uploading diagnostic events.

faq.question: Does this skill configure other Firebase products?
faq.answer: No. Its scope is Analytics setup, event logging, and screen tracking, not Auth, Firestore, Crashlytics, Hosting, or other Firebase products.
